Concave lenses are used to correct nearsightedness (myopia) and are also used in telescopes and other optical instruments to increase the field of view.

On the other hand, a convex lens, also known as a converging lens, is thicker in the middle than at the edges. It converges light rays that pass through it, making them come together or focus at a point. Convex lenses are used to correct farsightedness (hyperopia) and are also used in cameras, binoculars, and other optical instruments to focus light and form images.

The main difference between concave and convex lenses is the way they refract light. Concave lenses refract light away from the center, while convex lenses refract light towards the center. This difference in refraction determines the type of lens and its application in various optical devices.
